data.one_liner: Hardware‑backed biometric signatures and encryption for Flutter apps.
data.what_it_does: Provides cryptographic signing and decryption using keys stored in Secure Enclave, StrongBox or Windows Hello. Supports key attestation, multiple key aliases, and hybrid modes for platforms without native EC support.
use_when: You need verifiable, replay‑protected biometric authentication
Your backend must verify a cryptographic proof of identity
You want hardware‑backed key storage with attestation on Android or Secure Enclave on iOS/macOS
avoid_when: Only a simple boolean biometric unlock is required
Targeting platforms without hardware key support (e.g., older Android versions)
You prefer a lightweight solution without native setup
strengths: Hybrid modes allow encryption on platforms lacking native EC keys
Fine‑grained key policies and alias management
weaknesses: Large API surface; steep learning curve
Windows implementation limited (no security level reporting)
data.setup_notes: Add platform‑specific permissions (USE_BIOMETRIC, USE_FINGERPRINT) and Android keystore/StrongBox config; iOS entitlements for Secure Enclave; Windows Hello capability flag. No code‑gen required.

alternatives.name: local_auth
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides simple biometric unlock without cryptographic keys

alternatives.name: passkeys
alternatives.why_pick_it: WebAuthn‑style passwordless auth, but lacks custom encryption APIs

alternatives.name: firebase_auth
alternatives.why_pick_it: Full auth backend with biometric optional, but not hardware‑backed signatures
